title: Under pressure? Exam stress and support at school
titleDe: Prüfungsstress und Unterstützung an der Schule

task.situation:
You are a member of your school’s student council. At the request of the school management, the council has carried out an online survey on exam stress among 240 students aged 15 to 18. The figures below are invented for this task as a simplified example.
Survey results:
• students who often or always feel under pressure before tests: 62% (15–16-year-olds: 53%, 17–18-year-olds: 71%)
• students who had three or more tests in the same week at least once last term: 48%
• main cause named: too many tests at the same time 41%, too little time to study 27%, pressure to get good marks 20%, not knowing how to study effectively 12%
• students who know whom to talk to at school when the pressure gets too much: 35%
• students who would take part in peer mentoring with older students: 58%
task.instruction: Write a report for the school management in which you:
points: present the main findings of the survey
explain the main causes of exam stress
recommend measures the school could take to support students

words.short: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Report der Schüler:innenvertretung an die Schulleitung über eine für die Aufgabe erfundene Online-Umfrage unter 240 Schüler:innen zu Prüfungsstress. Drei Inhaltspunkte: Ergebnisse präsentieren, Ursachen erklären, Maßnahmen empfehlen (z. B. Prüfungsplan, Lernzeit, Peer-Mentoring, Ansprechpersonen). Abschnitte mit Zwischenüberschriften, sachlich, vorsichtig formuliert, keine Kurzformen.

focus.label: impersonal reporting and hedging
focus.note: Marked: impersonal reporting phrases (according to the survey, it was found that, it is recommended that, it is suggested that) and hedging (appears to, seems to, tend to, may, might, is likely to, it would seem, it would appear that, the results suggest/indicate that). ‘Could’ and ‘should’ in recommendations, numbers and general linking words are not marked.

gaps.q: Our support project needs a short English name. What do we call it?
gaps.qDe: Unser Unterstützungsprojekt braucht einen kurzen englischen Namen, z. B. „Here to Help“. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: Which subject line do we put in the header?
steps.de: Die Betreffzeile sagt, worum es im Report geht.
steps.own: Short and factual: name the topic of the report and what it offers.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und sachlich: Thema des Reports und was er bietet.

options.label: Survey plus purpose
options.text: Survey on exam stress: findings and recommendations
options.why: Factual and complete: it names the survey and promises recommendations.

options.label: Topic and aim
options.text: Exam stress at school: survey results and ideas for support
options.why: Starts with the topic and shows that the report looks for solutions.

options.label: A precise focus
options.text: Pressure before tests: results of the student council survey

steps.q: Introduction: how do we open the report?
steps.de: Die Einleitung nennt Zweck und Datenquelle des Reports. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the introduction: who took part in the survey and what does the report do?
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Einleitung fertigschreiben: Wer hat an der Umfrage teilgenommen, und was leistet der Report?
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the introduction: who took part, what the report does and why the figures should be read with care.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Einleitung fertigschreiben: wer teilgenommen hat, was der Report leistet und warum man die Zahlen vorsichtig lesen muss.

options.label: State the aim
options.text:
### Introduction
{{The aim of this report is to}} present the findings of an online survey on exam stress {{in which}} 240 students aged 15 to 18 took part. {{It also outlines}} the main causes and recommends ways the school could help.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{The aim of this report is to}} present the findings of an online survey on exam stress {{in which}} 240 students aged 15 to 18 took part. {{It also outlines}} the main causes and recommends ways the school could help. {{All figures should be read with some caution:}} taking part was voluntary, {{so students who feel strongly about the topic [[may]] have been}} more likely to answer.
options.why: Purpose, data source and structure in a few sentences: a classic report opening.

options.label: Refer to the request
options.text:
### Introduction
{{Following a request from the school management,}} the student council carried out an online survey on exam stress among 240 students aged 15 to 18. {{This report summarises the findings,}} outlines the main causes {{and makes recommendations}} for the school.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{Following a request from the school management,}} the student council carried out an online survey on exam stress among 240 students aged 15 to 18. {{This report summarises the findings,}} outlines the main causes {{and makes recommendations}} for the school. {{One limitation should be kept in mind:}} the survey reflects only one point in the school year, {{so the figures [[might]] look}} different in a quieter period.
options.why: Names who asked for the report and what it covers, in a neutral tone.

options.label: Start with a reaction
options.reject: Too personal and emotional for a report: ‘I must say’, ‘I was really shocked’, ‘I personally think’ and ‘far too much pressure’. A report states its purpose and its data source in a neutral, impersonal tone.
options.rejectDe: Zu persönlich und emotional für einen Report („I was really shocked“, „I personally think“): Zweck und Datenquelle sachlich und unpersönlich nennen.
options.text:
### Introduction
As a member of the student council, I must say that I was really shocked by the results of our survey of 240 students. I personally think that the school puts far too much pressure on us, and I hope that this report will finally change something.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
As a member of the student council, I must say that I was really shocked by the results of our survey of 240 students. I personally think that the school puts far too much pressure on us, and I hope that this report will finally change something. The survey was voluntary, so the figures are perhaps not perfect, but they show how most of us really feel before a test.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: what are the main findings?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: die wichtigsten Ergebnisse der Umfrage. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add the missing figures from the survey in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die fehlenden Zahlen aus der Umfrage mit eigenen Worten ergänzen.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add the missing figures, compare the two age groups and give one possible reason for the difference.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die fehlenden Zahlen ergänzen, die beiden Altersgruppen vergleichen und einen möglichen Grund für den Unterschied nennen.

options.label: Report the figures
options.text:
### Key findings
The survey shows that 62 per cent of respondents often or always feel stressful before tests. Almost half (48 per cent) had three or more tests in one week last term. However, only 35 per cent know where they can become help at school when the pressure gets too much.
options.reject: Two typical mistakes: ‘feel stressful’ (→ feel stressed: a test is stressful, a person is stressed) and ‘become help’ (→ get help; ‘become’ means ‘werden’).
options.rejectDe: Zwei typische Fehler: feel stressful → feel stressed, become help → get help („become“ heißt „werden“).
options.textLong:
### Key findings
The survey shows that 62 per cent of respondents often or always feel stressful before tests. Almost half (48 per cent) had three or more tests in one week last term. However, only 35 per cent know where they can become help at school when the pressure gets too much. Of the two age groups, older students seem to feel the pressure more. While just over half of 15- and 16-year-olds (53 per cent) are regularly affected, the figure for 17- and 18-year-olds is 71 per cent. This may be explained by the extra workload before the school-leaving exams.

options.label: Figure by figure
options.text:
### Key findings
{{[[According to the survey]], over three in five respondents}} (62 per cent) often or always feel under pressure before tests, and 48 per cent had three or more tests in one week last term. {{Information about support, [[it would seem]], is lacking,}} as only 35 per cent know whom to talk to at school.
options.why: Each figure comes with a phrase that reports it neutrally, and the last point is carefully hedged.
options.textLong:
### Key findings
{{[[According to the survey]], over three in five respondents}} (62 per cent) often or always feel under pressure before tests, and 48 per cent had three or more tests in one week last term. {{Information about support, [[it would seem]], is lacking,}} as only 35 per cent know whom to talk to at school. {{When it comes to exam pressure, age [[appears to]] make a clear difference.}} Among 15- and 16-year-olds, 53 per cent report frequent pressure before tests, {{compared with 71 per cent of}} 17- and 18-year-olds. {{This gap [[may]] be due to}} the approaching school-leaving exams and a heavier workload.

options.label: Main finding first
options.text:
### Key findings
{{The results [[suggest that]] exam stress is}} common among students. {{[[It was found that]] 62 per cent of respondents}} often or always feel under pressure before tests, and 48 per cent had three or more tests in one week last term. {{However, only 35 per cent}} know whom to talk to at school.
options.why: A topic sentence sums up the results first, then the figures support it.
options.textLong:
### Key findings
{{The results [[suggest that]] exam stress is}} common among students. {{[[It was found that]] 62 per cent of respondents}} often or always feel under pressure before tests, and 48 per cent had three or more tests in one week last term. {{However, only 35 per cent}} know whom to talk to at school. {{Of the two age groups, older students [[seem to]] feel the pressure more.}} {{While just over half of 15- and 16-year-olds}} (53 per cent) are regularly affected, the figure for 17- and 18-year-olds is 71 per cent. {{This [[may]] be explained by}} the extra workload before the school-leaving exams.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: what causes exam stress?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: die Ursachen, die in der Umfrage genannt wurden. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain the causes from the survey in a neutral, general way.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Ursachen aus der Umfrage sachlich und allgemein erklären.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then explain the causes from the survey and what may lie behind them, in a neutral, general way, without examples of individual people.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Ursachen aus der Umfrage und ihre möglichen Hintergründe sachlich und allgemein erklären, ohne Beispiele einzelner Personen.

options.label: Rank the causes
options.text:
### Causes of exam stress
{{Asked what causes this pressure, 41 per cent named}} too many tests at the same time, followed by too little time to study (27 per cent). {{Pressure to get good marks [[appears to]] matter less}} (20 per cent), {{and only 12 per cent}} mentioned not knowing how to study effectively.
options.why: Goes through the causes from the most to the least frequent and hedges the interpretation.
options.textLong:
### Causes of exam stress
{{Asked what causes this pressure, 41 per cent named}} too many tests at the same time, followed by too little time to study (27 per cent). {{Pressure to get good marks [[appears to]] matter less}} (20 per cent), although it [[may]] have several sources: marks can decide whether students move up to the next year, and expectations at home [[seem to]] play a part. {{Only 12 per cent}} mentioned not knowing how to study effectively, {{which [[suggests that]]}} most students see the problem in the organisation of tests rather than in their own methods.

options.label: Explain the main cause
options.text:
### Causes of exam stress
{{Timing [[appears to be]] the main reason for this pressure.}} For 41 per cent, it is too many tests at once, {{and a further 27 per cent}} named too little time to study. {{This [[may]] be because}} afternoon lessons, sport and part-time jobs leave few free evenings.
options.why: Focuses on timing, the main cause, and offers possible explanations.
options.textLong:
### Causes of exam stress
{{Timing [[appears to be]] the main reason for this pressure.}} For 41 per cent, it is too many tests at once, {{and a further 27 per cent}} named too little time to study. {{This [[may]] be because}} afternoon lessons, sport and part-time jobs leave few free evenings. {{Study habits [[might]] also play a part,}} even though few students see them as a cause: many [[may]] never have learnt how to plan their revision. {{Those who leave everything until the last few days [[tend to]] feel}} more pressure, {{which [[suggests that]]}} study skills and stress are closely connected.

options.label: Cause by cause
options.text:
### Causes of exam stress
The answers point to several causes. The most frequent was too many tests at the same time (41 per cent). For example, 27 per cent named too little time to study. Otherwise, 20 per cent mentioned pressure to get good marks, and 12 per cent named not knowing how to study effectively.
options.reject: Two linkers do not fit: ‘For example’ introduces an example of the cause before, but too little time to study is a separate cause (→ In second place), and ‘Otherwise’ means ‘if not’, not ‘also’ (→ In addition).
options.rejectDe: Zwei Linking words passen nicht: „For example“ kündigt ein Beispiel an, aber zu wenig Lernzeit ist eine eigene Ursache, und „Otherwise“ heißt „sonst, andernfalls“, nicht „außerdem“.
options.textLong:
### Causes of exam stress
The answers point to several causes. The most frequent was too many tests at the same time (41 per cent), as several subjects often hold their tests in the same few weeks before the holidays. For example, 27 per cent named too little time to study. Otherwise, 20 per cent mentioned pressure to get good marks, which may be linked to the fact that marks decide whether students move up to the next year. Only 12 per cent named not knowing how to study effectively, so most students seem to look for the problem in the organisation of tests.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: what do we recommend?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Maßnahmen, die die Schule setzen könnte, passend zu den Ursachen aus der Umfrage. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the recommendations with concrete measures for the school.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Empfehlungen mit konkreten Maßnahmen für die Schule fertigschreiben.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the recommendations and explain in your own words how each measure would work at school.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Empfehlungen fertigschreiben und mit eigenen Worten erklären, wie jede Maßnahme an der Schule funktionieren würde.

options.label: Remove the causes
options.reject: These measures are not realistic: a school cannot simply abolish tests, marks and the school-leaving exams. They are not based on the survey either, which points to too many tests at the same time, not to tests as such.
options.rejectDe: Nicht realistisch und nicht aus der Umfrage abgeleitet: Die Schule kann Tests, Noten und Reifeprüfung nicht abschaffen, und die Befragten klagen über zu viele Tests auf einmal, nicht über Tests an sich.
options.text:
### Recommendations
In view of these results, it is recommended that the school abolish tests and marks altogether, so that students can learn without any pressure. Homework should no longer be set either, and the school-leaving exams could be replaced by a project of each student’s own choice. The time saved could be used for a weekly relaxation afternoon called ‘{SCHEME}’ with sport and music.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
In view of these results, it is recommended that the school abolish tests and marks altogether, so that students can learn without any pressure. Homework should no longer be set either, and the school-leaving exams could be replaced by a project of each student’s own choice. The time saved could be used for a weekly relaxation afternoon called ‘{SCHEME}’ with sport and music. Without marks, students would no longer compare themselves with their classmates, and teachers would have more time for interesting lessons instead of correcting tests. In this way, exam stress would disappear from the school completely.

options.label: A test calendar and mentors
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{With these causes in mind, [[it is recommended that]] the school}} introduce a shared online test calendar {{so that}} no class has more than two tests in the same week. {{Furthermore, a peer mentoring scheme called ‘{SCHEME}’ could be set up,}} as 58 per cent of respondents would take part. Older students could share study tips, and since students [[tend to]] talk openly to their peers, asking for help [[might]] become easier.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{With these causes in mind, [[it is recommended that]] the school}} introduce a shared online test calendar {{so that}} no class has more than two tests in the same week. {{Teachers could then}} plan their tests together, and students would know early when busy weeks are coming. {{Furthermore, a peer mentoring scheme called ‘{SCHEME}’ could be set up,}} as 58 per cent of respondents would take part. Older students could share study tips and show younger ones where to find the student advisers. Since students [[tend to]] talk openly to their peers, asking for help [[might]] become easier.
options.why: Tackles the most frequently named cause with a simple tool and uses the strong interest in peer mentoring.

options.label: Time and space to study
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{Given these causes, [[it is suggested that]] the school}} open a quiet study room in the afternoons during busy test weeks and spread test dates more evenly across the term. {{In addition, a short workshop on}} revision methods early in the school year {{[[is likely to]] help}} students who are unsure how to learn effectively. {{Finally, a support campaign called ‘{SCHEME}’}} could use posters to show students where to find help when tests pile up.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{Given these causes, [[it is suggested that]] the school}} open a quiet study room during busy test weeks and spread test dates more evenly across the term. {{In addition, a short workshop on}} revision methods early in the school year {{[[is likely to]] help}} students who are unsure how to learn effectively. {{Beyond these measures, support staff should be more visible,}} as only about a third of respondents know where to turn. The student advisers and the school psychology service could visit every class, {{and a support campaign called ‘{SCHEME}’,}} with posters listing their office hours, [[might]] make them easier to find.
options.why: Answers several causes at once: too little time, uncertain study methods and support that students do not know about.

steps.q: Conclusion: how do we end the report?
steps.de: Der Schluss greift Ergebnisse, Ursachen und Empfehlungen auf und schaut nach vorn. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete both sentences in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann beide Sätze mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then sum up the findings and causes in your own words and say what should happen next.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Ergebnisse und Ursachen mit eigenen Worten zusammenfassen und sagen, wie es weitergehen soll.

options.label: Sum up the main finding
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{To sum up, the survey [[indicates that]]}} exam stress is widespread and mostly has organisational causes. {{If the measures above are taken,}} exam periods [[are likely to]] become more manageable.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{To sum up, the survey [[indicates that]]}} exam stress is widespread, especially among older students, and that it mostly has organisational causes. Although the figures should be read with care, they point the school in a clear direction. {{If the measures above are taken,}} exam periods [[are likely to]] become more manageable for everyone.
options.why: Repeats the key finding in one hedged sentence and links it to the recommendations.

options.label: Look ahead
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{Overall, [[it would appear that]]}} test pressure is common and that students would welcome more structure and support. {{The student council would be glad to}} help put these recommendations into practice and repeat the survey next year.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{Overall, [[it would appear that]]}} test pressure is common, particularly in the final years, and that students would welcome more structure and support. {{The student council would be glad to}} help put these recommendations into practice. Repeating the survey in the same term next year would also show whether the measures have made a difference.
options.why: Ends with an offer and a clear next step, which suits a student council report.

checks.en: Header complete: To, From, Date and a factual subject line
Five sections, each with a clear subheading
The introduction states the purpose and who took part in the survey
All figures are taken correctly from the survey
All three content points: findings, causes, recommendations
Claims are hedged where the data cannot prove them (‘appears to’, ‘may’)
Formal and impersonal: no contractions, no personal stories

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Report auf B2-Niveau (SRDP) zu einer erfundenen Umfrage über Prüfungsstress und übt dabei, Ergebnisse unpersönlich zu berichten, Aussagen vorsichtig abzusichern (hedging) und Maßnahmen formell zu empfehlen.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen (ohne Karten: 1–4 Finger, die Tasten 1–4 wählen wie A–D), Beamer im Vollbild. Die Umfrageergebnisse aus der Aufgabe zusätzlich an die Tafel schreiben, sie werden in den eigenen Sätzen gebraucht. Vorab kurz klären: under pressure, respondents, peer mentoring, student advisers (Schüler:innenberater:innen), school psychology service (Schulpsychologie). Thema vorher ankündigen und Hilfsangebote bereithalten (siehe Hinweise).
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts), „Report“ als Überschrift. Darunter der Kopf wie am Beamer: To, From, Date, Subject (die Betreffzeile wird im ersten Schritt gewählt). Fünf Abschnitte (Introduction, Key findings, Causes of exam stress, Recommendations, Conclusion): jeder beginnt nach einer Leerzeile mit seiner Zwischenüberschrift auf einer eigenen Zeile (unterstrichen), darunter der Absatz; am Rand steht nichts. Wendungen für unpersönliches Berichten und vorsichtiges Formulieren grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: 6 Entscheidungen in beiden Längen: Betreff und fünf Abschnitte (jede Entscheidung ein ganzer Abschnitt). Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Ergebnisse lesen, 6 Entscheidungen à ca. 2 min, ca. 22 min Abschreiben, 5 min Checkliste, der Rest für die Fallen. Volltext lang (100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen, die Abschnitte sind länger, daher ca. 35–40 min Abschreiben und mehr Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen. Gerüst kurz (ca. 60 min): 4 min Aufgabe, pro Entscheidung 1 min, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben pro Abschnitt, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; in einer 50-Minuten-Stunde den Schluss als Hausübung und die Checkliste am Beginn der nächsten Stunde. Gerüst lang (100 min): gleicher Ablauf, aber 8–10 min eigenes Schreiben pro Hauptabschnitt (ca. 100 Wörter) und ca. 6 min für Einleitung und Schluss. Die Zahlen bleiben die ganze Stunde an der Tafel.
teacher.traps: Introduction C (LSR): persönlicher, emotionaler Ton („I must say“, „I was really shocked“, „I personally think“, „far too much pressure“) statt sachlicher Einleitung. Key findings A (LSA): feel stressful statt feel stressed, become help statt get help (false friend). Causes of exam stress C (CC): „For example“, obwohl zu wenig Lernzeit eine eigene Ursache und kein Beispiel ist (→ In second place), „Otherwise“ im Sinn von „außerdem“ (false friend zu „sonst“). Recommendations A (TA): unrealistische Forderungen (Tests, Noten und Reifeprüfung abschaffen), die die Schule nicht umsetzen kann und die nicht aus der Umfrage folgen. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Aufbau: Der Report hat in beiden Fassungen genau fünf Abschnitte mit Zwischenüberschrift (Einleitung, drei Hauptabschnitte, Schluss); die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen mit längeren Abschnitten (Grenzen der Umfrage in der Einleitung, Vergleich der Altersgruppen bei den Ergebnissen, mögliche Hintergründe der Ursachen, genauere Empfehlungen und ein ausführlicherer Schluss). Sensibles Thema: vorher ankündigen, dass es um Prüfungsstress geht, und sachlich bleiben. Die Umfrage ist erfunden; keine eigenen Erfahrungen abfragen, keine Einzelfälle besprechen, niemand muss etwas über sich erzählen. Auch die Gerüst-Aufträge verlangen nur allgemeine Erklärungen. Am Ende kurz zeigen, wo es echte Unterstützung gibt: Schüler:innenberater:innen und Vertrauenslehrer:innen an der Schule, die Schulpsychologie der Bildungsdirektion und Rat auf Draht (Telefon 147, rund um die Uhr, anonym und kostenlos). Hedging-Hinweis: Weil eine freiwillige Online-Umfrage nichts beweist, sind Formulierungen wie „appears to“ oder „may“ hier inhaltlich begründet und kein bloßer Stil. Differenzierung: Schnelle schreiben im Gerüst-Modus vier Sätze mit „maybe“ über den Unterschied zwischen den Altersgruppen und formulieren sie dann mit verschiedenen Hedging-Formen um (appears to, is likely to, may be due to, tend to). Hausübung: den Report mit anderen Entscheidungen neu schreiben oder dieselbe Aufgabe für eine erfundene Umfrage zum Thema Schlaf bearbeiten.
